contract: Durable tenant allowance in plain Ecto/Postgrex tables on PostgreSQL 16 under the state/tenant-isolation floor: numeric(38,0) counters committed, held and reserved per (tenant, window, unit), the window exactly {:period, id} with an opaque host ID, the amount of a unit derived at each reserve/3 from a domain/entitlement resolution (the sum of its non-settle_only allowances of a period_kind mapped to the window tag, every allowance's grant_id among the listed grants, settle_only exactly for a grace grant, unmapped units and kinds ignored); Run reservations of 1..16 sorted unique units all or none, idempotent by run_id (equal request digest duplicate, other digest conflict), counter rows locked one at a time in unit order at a checked READ COMMITTED Need, in the Piece's own transaction (caller transaction refused); grace reserves nothing (settle_only); settle/3 commits a known actual in full or holds the estimate for :unknown, also after expiry, release or revocation; reconcile/3 moves a held estimate out and commits an attributable actual with basis :metering or :write_off; release/3 frees an open reservation only before its expiry; status/3 reads counters and the derived amount and remaining, also with resolution nil. Own Cure laws for the per-unit decisions; fixed error atoms that echo no ID or amount; a database failure is unavailable and safe to retry. No clock, timer, carry-over, pricing, posting, metering read or Run control.
limits: The state/tenant-isolation limits apply: the table owner can turn forcing off or drop the policies, and a superuser or BYPASSRLS role ignores them, so production connects as a non-owner, non-bypass application role with the README grants. The consumer Repo's query telemetry still receives the scope parameters (the tenant).
READ COMMITTED is a consumer Need that the Piece checks (current_setting('transaction_isolation') before any table query) but cannot set.

The host chooses the window and supplies a current resolution: a resolution resolved before a revocation still admits until the host resolves again. A duplicate reserve reports the first result, so the host must not start a Run whose reservation it has released or settled.
Allowance is permission to spend, not the total charge: an actual can exceed its estimate, and committed may pass the amount.

Held and expired amounts stay counted until settled or reconciled; there is no timer. No rolling window, local month, carry-over, per-principal allowance, pricing or posting. The quota tables are not captured by state/audit-log.
domain/entitlement is a test-only dependency (the tests build resolutions with it); the library code does not call it, nor workflow/budget.
A database failure, including a lost connection, is {:error, :unavailable} and says nothing about whether the write committed; the outcome is left to a retry with the same request.

Concurrency, lock order, restart and row-security evidence are finite scenarios on one local PostgreSQL 16 with repeated runs, not proofs; the Cure laws cover only the per-unit decisions over the counter values Elixir supplies, and the row locks, the input computation and every SQL step are test-grounded.

grounding.claim: For all counters, amounts, settle_only flags and estimates, when admit/4 admits, committed + held + reserved <= amount after it.
For all counters, amounts and estimates, admit/4 with settle_only true admits nothing.
For all inputs, a refusal of admit/4 (settle_only or insufficient) returns the counters it was given, also counters already over the amount after an overage.
For all counters, estimates and release flags, settling Unknown adds exactly the estimate to held and leaves committed unchanged.
For all counters, estimates, actuals and release flags, settling Known(actual) adds the actual to committed in full and leaves held unchanged.

Pinned Cure checks the Counters, Admission and Outcome types and the production admit/4, settle/4, reconcile/3 and release/2 decisions (every function @total) with a clean audit: no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproven-total items. Breaking unknown_is_held or the settle_only branch makes the module fail to compile (negative controls run by temporary edit).

Listed scenarios on the worker's own disposable PostgreSQL 16 database with DBConnection.ConnectionPool Repos (not the Sandbox) connected as the ELZ-285 application role with only the README grants (fails when ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE is unset), in random schemas dropped afterwards; after every case each counter equals the sum over its unit rows (reserved the open estimates, held the estimates settled :unknown and not reconciled, committed the known and reconciled actuals). 1 two reservations of 6 against 10, held behind another connection's counter row lock until both wait in pg_locks, one applied and one insufficient, reserved 6; 2 a reserve, a settle and a release of units A and B all wait on A (pg_locks), each of the three started last in turn, still waiting after deadlock_timeout, all commit; 3 reserve duplicate also with a later now_ms and a grace resolution, at its expiry and with a resolution lacking the unit, conflict on estimate, window, expiry and unit set, stored digest equal to the SHA-256 of the README encoding built in the test, duplicate after release reserving nothing, settle, reconcile and release duplicates and conflicts, not_held and unknown_reservation; 4 unknown held, remaining not growing, a reservation that fits only without held insufficient, metering reconcile frees it; 5 open and held reservations survive stopping and restarting the Repo and then settle and write off with actor_ref and reason kept; 6 grace settle_only and settlement, settlement after revocation, resolution refusals (absent grant_id, another tenant, inconsistent settle_only, duplicate or empty grants, bad status and amount, missing key), other keys ignored, no_allowance, a hand-built two-grant resolution summing only the entitled allowance (10, settle_only false, 10 admitted, 1 more insufficient), a third grant_id refused, a grace-only unit settle_only, an unmapped local_month allowance ignored but refused under an unknown grant_id, an unmapped unit ignored, status with resolution nil; 7 November and December reservations concurrent and separate, a late November settlement leaving December unchanged; 8 expiry equal to now refused, release one before expiry, expired at expiry and kept, settlement after expiry and after release, already_settled; 9 overage committed in full, remaining 0, next reservation insufficient; 10 TenantIsolation.verify/3 for each table, no T2 row visible under T1, a T2 settle unknown_reservation, a direct T2 insert and DELETE on each table 42501; 11 a caller transaction gives in_transaction for every function with no query on the Repo, a repeatable read Repo gets isolation from every write with nothing committed, and a quota over a missing schema gets unavailable from every function, without a raise and with nothing committed; 12 inner and outer bounds of every text, run_id, reason, estimate count (1, 15, 16 with a repeat, 17), unsorted and duplicate units, amounts and actuals, unknown unit, ttl and window tag, new/1 and migration prefix refusals; 13 Cure laws, audit and decisions. Negative controls by temporary edit: dropping the reservation primary key fails case 3 (a second reservation is stored), reading the counter without FOR UPDATE fails case 1 (both admitted), settling :unknown as zero fails case 4, and locking settle/3's counters in reverse unit order fails case 2 with a deadlock that returns unavailable. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

PostgreSQL 16 row locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), deadlock detection after deadlock_timeout, READ COMMITTED re-reads after a lock wait, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waiting on a concurrent uncommitted insert, row-level security and numeric(38,0) are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2 results and rollback, in_transaction?/0 and Ecto.Migration.execute/1 are upstream behavior, reached through Elzoo.TenantIsolation.transact/3.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler, kernel and audit for the selected laws and the compiled decisions.
Elixir Erlang term order of atoms and tuples for the unit order, String.valid?/1, the utf8 binary pattern and integer arithmetic for the text rule and counters.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto.hash(:sha256, iodata) computes the request digest.

The consumer runs the migration as the table owner, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with only the README grants at READ COMMITTED, calls TenantIsolation.verify/3 for each quota table at startup, keeps code that holds the connection from calling set_config itself, supplies a current resolution and the window for each reservation, does not start a Run whose reservation it released or settled, and retries an unavailable result with the same request.

telemetry.contract: The Piece emits no event and no log; its queries pass log: false. The consumer Repo's query telemetry still receives the scope parameters, the tenant-isolation limit.

config.contract: The quota value from new/1 (exactly repo: and prefix: under the identifier rule) is a construction-time operand; fixed Contract bounds: 1..16 estimates, amounts and times 0..2^63-1 (estimates from 1), 1..128-byte texts, 1..200-byte run_id, 1..256-byte reason. No ambient or hot configuration.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; release/3 and reconcile/3 are data operations, and the consumer owns the Repo, the migrations and the database roles.
